ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is quadrilateral QPRS, point Q is at the upper left, P is at the lower left, R is at the upper right, S is at the lower right, and diagonal PR is drawn. The figure marks ∠PQR = 75°, ∠QRP = 30°, ∠RPS = 50°, and what is required is ∠PSR at point S. The problem also gives QR = PS. Reasoning: In triangle PQR, ∠QPR = 180° - 75° - 30° = 75°. Therefore ∠QPR = ∠PQR, and the sides opposite the two are equal, so QR = PR. Also because the problem gives QR = PS, so PR = PS. Thus triangle PRS is an isosceles triangle, and the vertex angle ∠RPS = 50°. So the base angles ∠PRS and ∠PSR are equal, both being (180° - 50°) / 2 = 65°. Therefore ∠PSR = 65°.

raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, $QR = PS$. What is the size of $\angle PSR$?

method.method_draft: Use angle chasing and isosceles-triangle facts. From the image, read quadrilateral QPRS with diagonal PR drawn, with ∠PQR = 75°, ∠QRP = 30°, ∠RPS = 50°, and the unknown angle at S is ∠PSR. In triangle PQR, compute ∠QPR = 180° − 75° − 30° = 75°. Since ∠QPR = ∠PQR, the opposite sides QR and PR are equal. From the text, QR = PS, so PR = PS. Therefore triangle PRS is isosceles with vertex angle ∠RPS = 50°, so the two base angles are equal: ∠PRS = ∠PSR = (180° − 50°)/2 = 65°.

method.method_draft: Use a sine-rule/trigonometric formulation. From the image, identify triangle PQR with angles 75° at Q and 30° at R, and triangle PRS with ∠RPS = 50° and unknown x = ∠PSR. In triangle PQR, the remaining angle at P is 75°, so by the sine rule PR/QR = sin 75°/sin 75° = 1, hence PR = QR. From the text, QR = PS, so PR = PS. In triangle PRS, apply the sine rule with angles x at S and 130° − x at R: PS/sin(130° − x) = PR/sin x. Since PS = PR, sin(130° − x) = sin x, giving x = 65° in the valid triangle-angle range.
